summary: Kickoff to align Citrine Logistics on Redwood activation runway: security, networking (VPC), pilot metrics, and a short perf benchmark. Customer leaning toward Dedicated for predictable throughput but wants clarity on VPC/private deployment and audit/KMS requirements.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-05 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~48m | Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Kapoor, Marcus Li (Redwood) — Lena Ortiz, Samir Patel, Ruth Nguyen (Citrine)

[00:00] Alex Chen: ok, hi everyone, thanks for joining. i'm alex from redwood, i handle large accounts, with priya and marcus here. quick intro round?
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: lena here, head of ml ops at citrine, thanks for having us. we own infra and model serving.
[00:17] Samir Patel: samir, director of platform, i'll be the network/security owner.
[00:21] Ruth Nguyen: ruth, cloud eng — i'll do the peering and infra bits.
[00:25] Priya Kapoor: priya, csm at redwood — i'll run onboarding tasks and keep timelines.
[00:30] Marcus Li: marcus, solutions eng, i'll help with perf, kernels, and the benchmark.

[02:04] Alex Chen: agenda — security checklist, deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private), pilot scope and metrics, timeline, and next steps. anything else to add?
[02:16] Lena Ortiz: maybe a little on SDKs and integration patterns — webhooks, async vs sync.
[02:19] Alex Chen: noted.

[04:02] Samir Patel: first big question from our side: we have sensitive PII in transcripts, need SOC2 + KMS encryption, and probably want VPC peering or on-prem. can you summarize options?
[04:18] Marcus Li: sure — we support three deployment models. hosted api for fast dev; dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput and isolation; and private (VPC or on-prem) for regulated data. for KMS we integrate with customer KMS/HSM and you keep keys. audit logs and long retention are available through the console.
[04:40] Samir Patel: will audit logs show token-level? we need traceability per request for compliance.
[04:46] Marcus Li: yes, token-level cost and latency breakdowns are in the console, and we export audit logs to your SIEM (s3 or splunk). sometimes the export path name gets mis-typed in docs — but we can share a concrete example.

[06:20] Ruth Nguyen: about networking — if we choose private deployment, are we managing the control plane or do you? which parts sit in our V P C?
[06:31] Marcus Li: with Redwood Private the control plane can be customer-managed; compute runs in your VPC and you manage peering. for dedicated we also offer VPC peering options. we have a short network checklist (ports, egress rules, CIDR ranges) — i'll send that.

[08:02] Lena Ortiz: performance — our expected qps is spiky: batch of 40-80 requests/min during peak hours, with sub-300ms token-latency target for chat flows. does dedicated handle that without big overprovisioning?
[08:18] Marcus Li: yes dedicated is for predictable throughput and you can configure autoscaling + burst. we also do automatic KV caching and prefix caching to reduce tokens and cost. for sub-300ms it depends on model size and quant — we'll run a baseline.
[08:40] Lena Ortiz: model size — we're evaluating a 7B finetuned model and an LLM ensemble for reranking.
[08:46] Alex Chen: good to know. caching + quant can help. we'll propose a quantization profile and a batch policy to balance latency vs unit cost.

[10:10] Samir Patel: security nit: SSO + SAML for console access and RBAC. also want to make sure data residency can be locked to eu-west if needed.
[10:21] Priya Kapoor: we support SSO/SAML and granular RBAC. data region pinning is available for private/dedicated. i'll attach the security whitepaper and the iso/soc certs after the call.
[10:36] Lena Ortiz: can you send SOC 2 type II artifacts? our compliance team will want them.
[10:40] Priya Kapoor: yes, SOC2 and ISO will be in the packet.

[12:05] Ruth Nguyen: integration — do you have an SDK for node and python? and how does streaming vs non-streaming work for callbacks?
[12:15] Marcus Li: node/python SDKs exist; streaming responses supported via server-sent events/websocket. we also support structured output and function-calling, though sometimes the auto-transcribe calls it function 'callin' in notes, sorry.

[14:00] Alex Chen: pilot proposal: 2-week pilot (week 1: deploy and baseline, week 2: perf tuning and production traffic ramp). success metrics: 95th latency under X ms, cost per 1k tokens under $Y, and no security gaps. thoughts?
[14:18] Lena Ortiz: sounds right, would add error rate under 1% and throughput headroom of 20% for bursts.
[14:26] Samir Patel: agree. also would like a runbook for failover — what happens if a model variant is down, do you have fallback routes?
[14:34] Marcus Li: yes — smart routing with automated fallback to compatible model variants; we can define canary policies and automatic fallback thresholds.

[16:05] Ruth Nguyen: about billing and cost controls — can we get per-route quotas and token caps during pilot to avoid surprise bills?
[16:12] Alex Chen: yes, we have token quotas, per-route throttles and alerting in the console. we'll provide suggested guardrails.

[18:00] Lena Ortiz: any gotchas for on-prem package? we have a partly offline environment for some sites.
[18:08] Marcus Li: on-prem works but offline installs need some initial connectivity for license handshake; also some optimizations (kernel selection, GPU drivers) are sensitive to host setup. we'll share an installation checklist for air-gapped installs.

[20:25] Samir Patel: do you support customer-managed keys (CMK)? we require that for PII.
[20:31] Marcus Li: yes, CMK via KMS/HSM is supported. sometimes the docs show 'kms/h m s' spaced weirdly in transcripts, but it's real.

[22:50] Alex Chen: i want to align timelines — propose kickoff tasks: 1) share runbook and security pack by monday, 2) set perf window for baseline (2 hours) next thursday, 3) create pilot metrics doc and agree on thresholds.
[23:07] Priya Kapoor: i'll own the pilot metrics doc and invite citrine stakeholders.
[23:10] Lena Ortiz: good. we'll confirm the perf window once i coordinate with SRE.

[25:40] Ruth Nguyen: small question — how are logs exported? we prefer self-hosted s3 and Kafka.
[25:49] Marcus Li: we support s3 export and streaming to kafka via connector. we can do encrypted exports.

[28:00] Samir Patel: competitor question: we've evaluated vertex and another provider. how should we think about TCO here?
[28:12] Alex Chen: two pieces — unit economics and operational costs. Redwood Optimize recommends batching/quant/kv cache settings per workload and we'll show sample TCO for your traffic pattern. dedicated reduces per-token variance and helps predict costs vs managed endpoints which may spike.

[30:05] Lena Ortiz: i'd like a sample TCO spreadsheet and an example config for caching and batch sizes for a 7B model.
[30:12] Alex Chen: noted — will include that in the packet.

[32:45] Ruth Nguyen: are there known latency regressions with certain quant types?
[32:52] Marcus Li: quantization tradeoffs exist. int8 sometimes increases token throughput but can hurt retrieval quality — we'll run those tests in the baseline and provide recommended quant profiles.

[35:10] Samir Patel: support SLAs — do you offer uptime SLAs for dedicated?
[35:16] Alex Chen: dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; private/on-prem SLAs are part of enterprise licensing.

[36:40] Lena Ortiz: ok, action items recap?
[36:45] Priya Kapoor: recap: alex shares runbook & security docs; marcus schedules perf window and run baseline; priya creates pilot metrics doc; ruth shares VPC details and firewall egress list; citrine to confirm perf window and stakeholders.

[38:05] Samir Patel: timeline — assuming docs and network info arrive next week, pilot could start the week of 6/16?
[38:12] Alex Chen: that's feasible. we'll aim for pilot start 6/16 pending perf scheduling.

[40:00] Lena Ortiz: last question on data retention: can we set retention policy per project?
[40:06] Marcus Li: yes retention is configurable per workspace; we also support retention hold for investigations.

[42:15] Ruth Nguyen: please include a sample terraform snippet for peering if available.
[42:20] Marcus Li: will share terraform + cloudformation examples; sometimes the docs have a typo in terraform provider name but we'll send validated samples.

[44:00] Alex Chen: great — thanks all. i'll send the packet and next steps; priya will follow up on calendar invites. any blockers from citrine?
[44:10] Lena Ortiz: none immediate, just need the docs and perf slot.
[44:14] Samir Patel: same here.
[44:18] Ruth Nguyen: i'll gather the VPC/CIDR details and share by friday.

[45:00] Alex Chen: perfect. thanks everyone — meeting adjourned.

End notes: shared artifacts to be sent — onboarding-runbook.pdf, security-whitepaper.pdf, sample-tco.xlsx, perf-baseline-checklist.md, terraform-peering-example.tf. Links: security packet placeholder https://redwood.ai/security-pack/CITR-2025, onboarding runbook placeholder https://redwood.ai/onboarding/runbook-citrine.

Transcription notes: occasional mis-attributed lines, some acronyms transcribed with spaces (e g: V P C, K M S). Natural speech, overlaps and filler words preserved.
